title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes

method_excerpt:
To obtain an accurate description of LPSCl surfaces and their interactions with coating molecules, we fine-tuned a PET-MAD model on a material-specific dataset containing 8058 structures. Fine-tuning was performed by low-rank adaptation (LoRA), [30] in which the pretrained weights are kept fixed and low-rank corrections to them are optimized. Reference energies and forces were obtained from single-point DFT calculations using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) code [38] with the renormalized Strongly Constrained and Appropriately Normed (r2SCAN) functional. [69, 25, 20]

All simulations used the fine-tuned PET-MAD potential. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed in LAMMPS [73] with a time step of 1 fs and a Nosé–Hoover thermostat. ...

Adsorption models were built by placing protonated and lithiated carboxylate, sulfonate, and phosphonate molecules of controlled chain length approximately 5 Å above the relaxed LPSCl \{111\} surface (468-atom slab, lateral cell of 20.3\times 17.6 Å2), in the vacuum region, with the head group oriented toward the surface. The surface–adsorbate systems were relaxed by 500 ps of NVT dynamics at 300 K followed by minimization, after which adsorption energies were evaluated (SI Sec. S1.6). With 1, 9, or 18 adsorbed molecules, these systems contain 490-1310 atoms.

Water penetration was simulated by placing a pre-relaxed liquid water layer of 92 molecules approximately 5 Å above the coated surface, followed by 1 ns of MD simulation at 300 K (750–1590 atoms in total). Water molecules whose oxygen reached an \mathrm{O} –Li distance below 2.5 Å were counted as penetrating the coating; the resulting areal density, normalized by that of the uncoated LPSCl surface, gives the relative water accessibility, which provides a dynamic accessibility metric rather than a reaction energy.

Prelithiated acids were obtained by dissolving the acid in double-distilled (DD) water followed by stoichiometric addition of 1 N LiOH to neutralize each acidic proton. LPSCl coated with different acids was prepared by wet mixing the corresponding acids at specific molar percentages relative to LPSCl, in order to keep the ratio between the acid head group and the electrolyte surface area constant. ...

The ionic conductivity of LPSCl, both with and without additives, was evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at 25 °C using a BioLogic VSP‑300 potentiostat. ...

\mathrm{H_{2}S} evolution was measured using a home-built setup consisting of a plastic desiccator, a modular humidity generator (MHG32-ProUmid) and a \mathrm{H_{2}S} sensor (MODBUS RS485). After stabilization of the relative humidity (RH) at 20% the \mathrm{H_{2}S} evolution was measured.
blind_brief: 硫化物固态电解质（如银柱石型 Li6PS5Cl）离子电导率高、易于加工，是全固态电池的热门候选材料。但它对水分极其敏感，即使在干燥间里也会与水反应，释放有毒的 H2S 气体，同时材料本身发生降解。用分子涂层包覆颗粒表面是一种可放大的防护思路。然而，究竟哪些分子特征决定涂层与表面的结合强度，哪些决定涂层的阻水能力，目前仍缺乏系统认识。尤其是头基化学的系统比较，以及烷基链长的影响，此前几乎无人研究。本研究把机器学习势驱动的大尺度分子动力学与针对性实验结合起来。计算部分：以 r2SCAN 数据对基础势 PET-MAD 做 LoRA 微调，在 LPSCl 表面构建吸附模型。模型中放置质子化或锂化的羧酸、磺酸、膦酸分子，系统改变链长和吸附分子数（1、9、18 个），计算吸附能；再在涂层上方放置液态水层，进行纳秒级模拟，以"相对水可及性"量化水分子接近表面 Li 的程度。实验部分：用 THF 湿法将不同酸及其预锂化盐包覆在 LPSCl 上，通过阻抗谱测离子电导率，并在 20% 相对湿度下监测 H2S 释放；另用 FTIR、Raman、TGA 等手段辅助表征。请学员据此预判各变量可能产生的影响，并思考计算与实验应如何相互印证。

review_excerpt:
To assess the benefit of pretrained initialization, the same PET architecture was also trained from random initialization using the same material-specific dataset and evaluated on the same held-out test set. For this comparison, the model trained from scratch and the LoRA fine-tuned model were trained with identical data and settings (learning-rate schedule, batch of 850 atoms, cutoff, loss weights and random seed); the only difference is the initialization. Both models were trained for more than 1400 epochs, with a checkpoint saved every 50 epochs. For each training approach, the reported model is not the last checkpoint but the one with the lowest validation loss among all checkpoints up to epoch 1100 (epoch 900 for the model trained from scratch and epoch 1100 for the fine-tuned model). Note also that beyond 1100 epochs the model trained from scratch starts to overfit: its training error keeps decreasing faster than the validation error. On the other hand, the fine-tuned model is converged at this point: the validation energy and force RMSEs of all later checkpoints up to epoch 1500 differ from those of the selected checkpoint by less than 0.4 meV atom-1 and 0.6 meV Å-1, respectively. As shown in Fig. S1, fine-tuning reduces the energy RMSE from 7.26 to 4.53 meV atom-1 (about 25%) and the corresponding MAE from 4.33 to 2.83 meV atom-1. The force errors of the two models are of similar magnitude, with RMSEs of 82.90 meV Å-1 (scratch) and 78.17 meV Å-1 (fine-tuned) and MAEs of 45.6 and 47.8 meV Å-1, respectively. The small difference in force RMSE comes mainly from a few large errors (enlarged markers in Fig. S1d): the largest force-component errors of the model trained from scratch reach 7.4 eV Å-1, mostly on O atoms in a single test structure: an off-stoichiometric Li–O–P slab containing O–O bonded species, with DFT forces of up to 15 eV Å-1 on these atoms. This chemistry is represented by only 15 of the 6448 training structures, none with the same composition, and the fine-tuned model predicts all atoms of this structure with errors below 1.4 eV Å-1. Excluding the 20 atoms with the largest errors, the force RMSEs of the two models are 74.4 (scratch) and 76.1 meV Å-1 (fine-tuned). The fine-tuned model also converges faster and more smoothly: after 100 epochs its validation energy RMSE is 9.6 meV atom-1, compared with 33.5 meV atom-1 for the model trained from scratch, which needs about 500 epochs to reach a similar value (11.0 meV atom-1; values averaged over 20 epochs). Overall, fine-tuning lowers the energy error, gives fewer extreme force outliers and converges much faster, while typical force errors remain of similar magnitude. Fine-tuning therefore improves both energy and force accuracy across all local environments and should replace training from scratch for any solid-electrolyte system. This suggests that the representations acquired during pretraining on the broad MAD dataset [53] provide a useful prior for local environments that are only sparsely represented in the material-specific dataset, rather than requiring all relevant local interactions to be learned from scratch.
